## How zö agency prices

**9a.** zö agency is value-based. It wins on scope, reputation, ideas, portfolio and staff. Hourly rates and time and materials stay out of the pitch.

**9b.** A proposal shows a price for each item or phase, then the total. Descriptions say what the client gets, at the level of the deliverable. Hours, staffing math and rates by role stay out.

**9h.** Keep each price under what the market would expect for the same work. zö agency aims to be the strong choice at a fair price.

## RFP pricing rules

**9c.** When an RFP asks for rates, zö agency gives one blended rate: $275 an hour for every role. It never gives rates by role.

**9e.** When the RFP prints a budget, come in under it.

**9g.** When the RFP gives no budget, price catalog items at their Pricing Book price.

**9i.** The nonprofit discount is 12% and elective. When it's used, the proposal names it as a nonprofit discount.

**9j.** The City of Bend contract rate is $250 an hour, by negotiation. Any other negotiated rate is Sonja's call.

## Standing rules

**8a.** Revisions: 2 rounds included, and the 3rd round is a final review. More rounds bill at $275 an hour, quoted in a change order. Logo tiers keep their own round counts: Bronze 2 color rounds, Silver 3, Gold 4.

**8b.** Rush: Sonja decides the trigger and the charge. It's mostly used to train a client out of a habit.

**8c.** Travel day: $1,000 per person per day, client price.

**8d.** Hosting: clients pay Flywheel directly. zö agency doesn't resell hosting.

**8e.** Nonprofit discount: 12%, elective. When it's used, the proposal names it as a nonprofit discount.

**8f.** Annual escalator clauses: none.

## Approved wording

### Monthly Retainer

- Invoices go out on the 15th of the month before service and are due by the 1st of the service month.
- Account management, project management and Agency Director oversight are included.
- Two revision rounds are included per deliverable, plus a final review. Added rounds bill at $275 an hour, quoted in a change order first.
- Ad spend and boost spend run on [client]'s card on the ad account.
- Card payments carry a 3% processing fee. ACH payments carry no fee.
- Rates hold for the contract term.

### Fixed Quote, private client

- 50% is due on signing, 25% at [midpoint milestone] and 25% at completion.
- The deposit is due on receipt, before work starts. The remaining invoices are Net 15.
- Two revision rounds are included per deliverable, plus a final review. Added rounds bill at $275 an hour, quoted in a change order first.
- Card payments carry a 3% processing fee. ACH payments carry no fee.

### Government contract

- Invoices go out on the last day of each month, Net 15 unless the contract sets other terms.
- [The rest of the lines for the engagement type.]

### Time & Materials, Time & Deliverables, Not to Exceed

- zö agency bills actual time at $275 an hour, invoiced at approval or completion, Net 15.
- Materials pass through at cost. Deliverables such as print carry the price quoted in the estimate.
- Not to Exceed only: the total stays at or under $[cap]. zö agency tells [client contact] when work reaches 80% of the cap, before any work past the cap.

### Production

- 100% is due on receipt, before production starts.

### Outside the price

> Outside the [retainer / quote]: [ad spend, which runs on [client]'s card on the ad account; PR and media relations; printing; new photo or video shoots; any website rebuild]. Each gets a written estimate you approve before work starts.

### Travel

- Included: "Travel for [event or meeting] is included."
- Billed separately: "Travel is $1,000 per person per travel day."
- Government travel rules required by the RFP: "Travel bills at cost under [the RFP's rule, such as GSA rates], with written approval before booking."

### Nonprofit discount

Only when Sonja approves it. Add it as a line in the budget table above the total:

| Nonprofit discount (12%) | −$[monthly] | −$[total] |

### Change orders

> Work outside this scope gets a written change order with the price before it starts.

### Rates

> zö agency bills a blended rate of $275 an hour for every role.

If the RFP's pricing form asks for a rate per role, enter $275 on every line. zö agency never gives rates by role and never proposes time and materials as its way of working. The budget stays priced by item or phase.

### Tagline

"We are more than your agency. We are your strongest advocate." Exempt from the negation-contrast rule, per Brand and Writing Standards Section 10. Use it as written.

## Budget page guide

### Scope page

- **Overview.** Two short paragraphs. First: who zö agency will be for the client, the term, and who runs the account by name (Haley Neff day to day, Sonja Anderson throughout). Second: the meeting and reporting rhythm, and what goes to the client for approval before it goes live.
- **Workstreams.** One subhead per RFP scope item, in the RFP's order and words. Under each, bullets that name a deliverable with its frequency or count: "Publish about 13 posts a month," "Send a monthly sponsor newsletter, eight issues from January through August." End each workstream with its approval checkpoint where one applies.
- Say what zö agency does. Where a vendor or the client does the work (hosting, cashless payment systems, ticketing platforms), say "coordinate with."
- Name what runs on the client's account: ad spend, boost spend, hosting.

### Timeline page

- **Phase table.** Columns: #, Phase, Work, Timing. Timing uses real dates or "weeks X to Y from award." Dates in US format: April 19, 2027.
- **Workstream plan table.** Columns: #, Workstream, Measure, Plan. One row per workstream. The measure is the number the client will see in reports.
- Check event dates against the calendar. National Garlic Day, for example, is April 19 every year.
- The close-out report lands inside the contract term, or the page says when it lands.

### Budget page

- **16a-style intro.** One paragraph: the engagement type, the term, and what the price covers, including account management, project management, Agency Director oversight and reporting.
- **One sentence on how the price behaves**, such as "The fee stays the same every month."
- **Headline line in bold:** "Monthly agency retainer: $X a month, [term]. Total $Y." or "Project total: $Y."
- **Table.** A price per item or phase, then the total. Columns: #, Service, Monthly, Contract total (retainer) or #, Service or Phase, Price (fixed quote). Service names match the scope page subheads. Bold total row.
- **Value descriptions.** Describe what the client gets, at the level of the deliverable. Name counts only where they protect the scope, such as revision rounds or the number of concepts. Hours, rates and staffing math stay off the page.
- **Included items** that a reader might assume cost extra, such as travel.
- **Outside the price**, from `standard-blocks.md`.
- **Writer notes** for options Sonja decides, such as the nonprofit discount, with the replacement lines ready to paste.
- The page shows prices.

### Fix elsewhere in the proposal

Check the draft's other pages for conflicts with the methodology and list each fix with a code (N1, N2): invoicing dates, markups, escalators, revision counts, travel terms, contract period, wrong dates, and scope promises zö agency can't keep (for example, "implement" work a vendor does). Quote the old line and give the new one.

### Writing rules that catch old proposal copy

Old drafts carry these. Rewrite them every time.

- "seamless extension," "innovative campaigns," "dynamic partnership," "agile team structure," "meaningful results": empty words. Name the person, the meeting rhythm, the deliverable.
- "not by boxes checked," "we're not rebuilding anything," "rather than": negation-contrast. Say what zö agency will do.
- "by far the most cost effective," "we're certain we'll be in line": hedging and boasting. State the price.
- "The Calendar that ties it together," "Five Pillars, One Calendar, One Report," "Use your archive as the engine": editorial headings. Label them: "Program timeline," "Workstream plan," "Archive-based content."
- "scope" and "workshop" as verbs: process verbs. "We'll price each project," "we'll hold a working session."
- Em dashes: none, ever.
- zö agency: lowercase, umlaut, every time.
- Contractions and future tense: "we'll," "you'll," "it's."

## Lines to replace in old drafts

| Old line | Replace with |
|---|---|
| "Invoices are issued early each month, by the seventh to ninth day" | The billing line for the engagement type |
| "Media, talent fees, print, stock, and third-party software are billed at cost with no markup" | "Ad spend runs at cost on your account." Print, talent and stock are priced in the estimate. |
| "Annual adjustments are limited to CPI" | Delete. zö agency contracts carry no escalator. |
| "zö agency is by far the most cost effective partner... we're certain we'll be in line with any other similar proposal" | Delete. State the price and what it covers. |
| "Each of yours will be scoped every time" | "Work outside this budget gets a written estimate you approve first." |
| "Three rounds of review and revision" | Two rounds plus a final review |
